title: NimbusPay merchant-assist kickoff + measurable outcomes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the kickoff plan, workshop agenda, scope, and concrete measurable success criteria for the NimbusPay Merchant Assist pilot. Goal is to validate that Redwood Inference can power a real-time, low-latency assistant that helps merchant support agents triage charge disputes and refund workflows with end-to-end traceability and acceptable unit economics.

Background / context (brief):
- NimbusPay: mid-market payments provider (~120k merchants). Goal: reduce average handle time (AHT) for merchant support and reduce refund leakage.
- Pilot ask: 6-week technical + product pilot integrated into agent UI for a cohort of 50 merchants (sandbox).
- Constraints: live transaction data contains PII; NimbusPay requires tenant isolation, KMS-managed keys, and audit logs.

Scope (what we will deliver in pilot):
- Inference endpoint: Redwood-hosted model chain (intent classification -> evidence extraction -> draft response generation).
- UI integration: simple iframe-based assistant mock inside NimbusPay agent view (webhook style).
- Data flows: sample transaction and dispute events streamed to our sandbox, with PII tokenization via NimbusPay staging KMS.
- Monitoring: latency, tokens/call, model version, per-request trace id, error rates surfaced in Redwood Console.
- Eval harness: 250 representative dispute prompts and 50 live-ish support transcripts for quality checks.

Out-of-scope (pilot):
- Full production rollout, SLA commitments, multi-tenant on-prem deployment.
- Deep retraining on NimbusPay data (we will use prompt engineering + small context augmentation only).

Key success metrics (quantitative) — MUST be measurable by end of pilot:
- Agent time savings: >= 20% reduction in average handle time (AHT) on test cohort compared to baseline (baseline AHT = 7.5 min).
- Draft accuracy: >= 85% of assistant drafts rated "usable without edits" by support agents in blind review (n >= 100).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile response < 450 ms for generation step (end-to-end assistant latency target from click to visible draft <= 800 ms).
- Cost target: average token cost per support interaction <= $0.03 (model + infra amortized across pilot).
- Safety/PII compliance: 0 incidents of unmasked PII leaving the sandbox; all requests must include tokenized identifiers when applicable.
- Reliability: system availability > 99% during business hours for the pilot window.

Acceptance criteria (end-to-end tests):
- AC1: Given a dispute transcript, assistant produces a suggested response and list of relevant evidence lines; human reviewer marks it usable for >=85% of sampled cases.
- AC2: API responses include trace_id and model_version; traces appear in Redwood Console correlating to sample IDs.
- AC3: Latency test script (1000 simulated requests spread over 1 hour) shows p95 < 450 ms for generation service and error rate <1%.
- AC4: Security review signoff: NimbusPay sec has validated KMS integration and audit logging config (ticket: NPAY-SEC-12 closed).

Workshop (kickoff) agenda — 90 minutes (T+0 week):
- 0:00–0:10 Introductions + objectives (Sofia / Nimbus product lead)
- 0:10–0:25 Technical architecture walkthrough (Marcus + Nimbus infra) — endpoints, tokenization, routing policies
- 0:25–0:40 Data & privacy constraints (Rina) — sample data scope, PII tokenization, retention windows
- 0:40–0:55 Quality expectations + evaluation plan (Kai) — eval harness, labeling process, sampling cadence
- 0:55–1:10 Operational runbook + monitoring (Elena) — alerts, rollback, incident playbooks
- 1:10–1:25 Implementation plan & sprint cadence (mutual) — integrations, front-end hooks, user study logistics
- 1:25–1:30 Next steps + owners recap

Roles & owners (initial):
- Customer lead: Priya Shah (NimbusPay PM) — overall pilot sponsor, acceptance decision
- Redwood SE lead: Sofia Martinez — kickoff lead, primary contact for product/metrics
- Infra / integration: Marcus Liu — KMS + sandbox networking, ingress rules, sample payload contract
- Quality & eval: Kai Thompson — dataset, annotation instructions, manual review coordination
- Security reviewer: Rina Patel — runs sec checklist and holds NPAY-SEC-12
- SRE on-call: Elena Novak — monitoring, alert thresholds, incident response

Data & security checklist (minimum items):
- Tenant isolation: sandbox account per merchant cohort, no mixing of production credentials
- KMS: customer-provided staging key for tokenization/pseudonymization (verify CMK rotation policy)
- Data retention: discard raw transcripts after 30 days unless opt-in for annotation (tracked)
- Audit logs: every request stored with trace_id, model_version, timestamp, and low-level token usage (redacted in exported reports)
- Access control: narrow IAM roles for the pilot team; no broad admin keys in dev machines

Instrumentation & observability plan:
- Redwood Console: per-route p95 latency, token counts, success/error breakdown, per-customer dashboards (sandbox cohort)
- Custom dashboards: NimbusPay support metrics (AHT, CSAT) pulled daily; correlation tests between assistant usage and AHT drop
- Alerting: p95 > 600 ms, error rate >2%, disk or queue backpressure alerts to SRE channel

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: Quality regression mid-pilot due to prompt drift or updated model weights. Mitigation: pin model_version + maintain small fallback (lighter model) with automated canary.
- Risk: PII leak in free-text fields. Mitigation: pre-send tokenization + post-response scrubber + manual audits on sample of outputs.
- Risk: Integration takes longer than planned. Mitigation: parallelize front-end iframe mock and backend wiring; deliver a "read-only" UI early for user testing.

Milestones & timeline (6-week outline):
- Week 0: Kickoff workshop; security checklist agreed; sample data contract signed
- Week 1: Endpoint and tokenization integration; sandbox data pushed; first synthetic load tests
- Week 2: Eval harness seeded with 250 prompts; internal QA review cycle 1
- Week 3: UI integration (iframe) + alpha user study with 10 agents
- Week 4: Iteration on prompts and guardrails; cost profiling and batching tweaks
- Week 5: Broader agent study (50 merchants cohort); collect annotations and AHT metrics
- Week 6: Final eval, handover meeting, remediation items + decision (go/no-go)

Deliverables (by end of pilot):
- Runbook + integration guide (Confluence)
- Eval report: quality matrix, sample failure cases, annotated transcripts
- Cost analysis: per-interaction breakdown and recommended config for Dedicated or Hosted pricing
- Handover checklist for production rollout (if accepted)

Open questions / decisions needed (for kickoff):
- What is the canonical baseline AHT cohort for Nimbus (need segment id)? Assigned: Priya. Due: +3 days.
- Will Nimbus permit annotation of up to 5% of live interactions? Security approval required. Assigned: Nimbus sec. Due: +5 days.
- Which model family are we allowed to use in sandbox? (redwood-llama-13b-q4 or a smaller family) Decision: Redwood/Customer to agree by EOD week0.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Redwood: prepare sandbox endpoint and sample payload schema (Marcus) — deliver by 2025-11-10
- Nimbus: export 250 sanitized transcripts and designate merchant cohort (Priya) — deliver by 2025-11-12
- Joint: schedule security review meeting (Rina + Nimbus sec) — calendar invite by 2025-11-07

Notes / scratch items (working):
- Keep an eye on tokenization cost — if tokenization adds too much latency consider pre-tokenized blobs with short-lived tokens.
- Consider enabling caching for repeated lookup of merchant policy snippets (saves token cost + latency).
- Label taxonomy: {"usable_without_edit","needs_minor_edit","not_usable"} — Kai to author detailed labeling guide.

Annotations & references:
- See linked artifacts (JIRA/Confluence/GitHub).
- Quick prototyping repo: github.com/redwood-inference/nimbuspay-adapter (branch: se/pilot-iframe)

Version history (brief):
- 2025-11-05: initial draft (Sofia)
- 2025-11-12: added security checklist and sample milestones (Rina, Marcus)
- 2026-03-01: updated success metrics and latency target after bench adjustments (Sofia)

End of doc.
